svg.title: Base Case: $97,500 Revenue to 42.5% Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-owner-profit; chart type: waterfall; title: Base Case: $97,500 Revenue to 42.5% Owner Net; subtitle: Opening gross revenue, four deductions, and one closing total.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Canonical annual revenue and margin are fixed; expense categories are an illustrative allocation of their difference. The first bar is the opening total, the middle four are signed deltas, and the sixth is the closing total, not another delta. Recurring overhead plus contractors equals $36,000 annually or $3,000 monthly, inside the $500–$4,000 monthly opex range. Deal-specific costs and realized capital losses are separate.; caption: $97,500 - $24,000 - $12,000 - $10,500 - $9,562.50 = $41,437.50, exactly 42.5% of revenue and displayed as $41,438 annual owner net profit. The owner works the core full-time seat; no additional owner salary is deducted. Returned principal never enters the opening revenue bar.; stages: label: Realized operator revenue; value: $97,500 annual gross; principal receipts excluded; numeric value: 97500.0; detail: Opening total contains realized interest, penalties, and positive disposition gains. Gross property sale proceeds and recovered certificate basis are not recognized as revenue in this operator scorecard.; label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $24,000 annual recurring operating overhead; numeric value: -24000.0; detail: Allocate $2,000 monthly to portfolio administration, data access, insurance, bookkeeping, secure records, and servicing systems; contractor retainers are separately shown in the next deduction.; label: Two contracted core seats; value: Subtract $12,000 annual contractor retainer expense; numeric value: -12000.0; detail: Budget $6,000 annually for title review retainers and $6,000 for local counsel retainers. These are limited service budgets, not full-time salaries; exceptional matter charges belong in deal-specific expenses.; label: Deal-specific execution costs; value: Subtract $10,500 in nonrecurring transaction costs; numeric value: -10500.0; detail: Allocate auction charges, targeted parcel inspections, recording expenses, incremental notices, and exceptional legal work here. Exclude costs already deducted when calculating a disposition gain to prevent double counting.; label: Realized capital losses; value: Subtract $9,562.50 of unrecovered investment basis; numeric value: -9562.5; detail: Recognize documented unrecovered basis from resolved loss positions. Do not expense every principal purchase or treat principal repayment as income; a cash reserve transfer alone does not establish a realized loss.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $41,437.50 exact; $41,438 rounded annual owner net; numeric value: 41437.5; detail: Closing total equals $97,500 multiplied by 42.5%. This is owner operating profit before personal income tax, with no leverage or separate owner salary modeled.

text.title: Base Case: $97,500 Revenue to 42.5% Owner Net
text.tspan: Base Case: $97,500 Revenue to 42.5% Owner Net

circle.title: label: Realized operator revenue; value: $97,500 annual gross; principal receipts excluded; numeric value: 97500.0; detail: Opening total contains realized interest, penalties, and positive disposition gains. Gross property sale proceeds and recovered certificate basis are not recognized as revenue in this operator scorecard.

label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $24,000 annual recurring operating overhead; numeric value: -24000.0; detail: Allocate $2,000 monthly to portfolio administration, data access, insurance, bookkeeping, secure records, and servicing systems; contractor retainers are separately shown in the next deduction.

label: Two contracted core seats; value: Subtract $12,000 annual contractor retainer expense; numeric value: -12000.0; detail: Budget $6,000 annually for title review retainers and $6,000 for local counsel retainers. These are limited service budgets, not full-time salaries; exceptional matter charges belong in deal-specific expenses.

label: Deal-specific execution costs; value: Subtract $10,500 in nonrecurring transaction costs; numeric value: -10500.0; detail: Allocate auction charges, targeted parcel inspections, recording expenses, incremental notices, and exceptional legal work here. Exclude costs already deducted when calculating a disposition gain to prevent double counting.

label: Realized capital losses; value: Subtract $9,562.50 of unrecovered investment basis; numeric value: -9562.5; detail: Recognize documented unrecovered basis from resolved loss positions. Do not expense every principal purchase or treat principal repayment as income; a cash reserve transfer alone does not establish a realized loss.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $41,437.50 exact; $41,438 rounded annual owner net; numeric value: 41437.5; detail: Closing total equals $97,500 multiplied by 42.5%. This is owner operating profit before personal income tax, with no leverage or separate owner salary modeled.

text.title: Assumptions: Canonical annual revenue and margin are fixed; expense categories are an illustrative allocation of their difference. The first bar is the opening total, the middle four are signed deltas, and the sixth is the closing total, not another delta. Recurring overhead plus contractors equals $36,000 annually or $3,000 monthly, inside the $500–$4,000 monthly opex range. Deal-specific costs and realized capital losses are separate.
